Exemptions	10 ARTICLE I. Description SECTION ONE. Constitutional Authority The Beta Sigma Chapter is organized in accordance with the National Constitution and Bylaws of Phi Mu Alpha Sinfonia. SECTION TWO. Governing Documents The Beta Sigma Chapter shall be organized and shall function in accordance with the National Constitution and Bylaws of Phi Mu Alpha Sinfonia, the Province 38 Bylaws, and these Beta Sigma Chapter Bylaws. ARTICLE II. Probationary Membership SECTION ONE. Probationary Dues The probationary dues or payment plans for probationary members of the Beta Sigma Chapter shall be due the day of the national exam. If dues or a payment plan are not secured by that time, that member may not take the exam at that time. Should a probationary member utilize a payment plan, the plan must conclude on or before the date of Initiation so said member may acquire his Initiation materials. SECTION TWO. Family Lineage: Big Brother & Little Brother The Beta Sigma Chapter shall use a Big Brother system to assist with probationary members shall be due the day o before initiation and to establish a family lineage. Big Brothers are responsible for any questions that Little Brothers may have regarding fraternity traditions or customs. The Fraternity Education Officer should answer any questions pertaining to fraternity history. Big Brothers and Little Brothers will be determined at a meeting prior to the Ceremony for Pledging. If a collegiate member in good standing wishes to take on the role of Big Brother, he may volunteer himself to do so. The Fraternity Education Officer, while in office, may not volunteer to be a Big Brother. In the event that there are more volunteers than probationary members, a simple majority quorum vote shall decide who shall take on that responsibility. In the event that there are more probationary members than collegiate members, collegiate members may take on more than one Little Brother, using the aforementioned volunteering process. Big Brother and Little Brother relationships shall be officially announced at the Ceremony for Pledging, where Big Brothers will pin Little Brothers with probationary membership pins. ARTICLE III. Finance SECTION ONE. Chapter Dues In addition to national per capita tax detailed in Article X, Section One of the Bylaws, Title I: National of Phi Mu Alpha Sinfonia, each collegiate member of the Beta Sigma Chapter shall pay chapter dues of $36 per semester, due by the third chapter meeting of each academic semester. If dues are not paid or the member has not submitted a payment plan by the due date (including grace period – see Article III, Section Two of these bylaws), then that member will be on probation with the chapter (See Article VIII, Section Four of these bylaws for terms of Chapter Probation). If deemed necessary by a two-thirds quorum vote, the chapter may allow for a temporary increase or decrease in chapter dues. The chapter treasurer shall issue receipts to brothers upon their payment(s). SECTION TWO. Payment Plans Each member of the Beta Sigma Chapter shall either pay in full by the chapter deadline or use a pre-approved payment plan as detailed by the Treasurer. The Treasurer may implement an alternate payment plan with any individual member of the chapter with a full report to and approval of the executive committee. All payments on plans must be completed one week prior to the National Deadline for dues. All requests for consideration for an alternate payment plan must be submitted in typed format to the Treasurer prior to the payment due date. In accordance to the Guide to Money Management this Fraternity does not front dues. SECTION THREE. Chapter Accounts The Beta Sigma Chapter shall hold a checking account, which shall serve as the chapter treasury. The Beta Sigma Chapter shall also hold a savings account in which money shall be allocated for the use of national events, Lyrecrest trips, etc. Only the President, Vice President, if he so desires, the Treasurer, and the Faculty Advisor, if he so desires, shall have access to the chapter accounts. Access shall be defined as having their name on the account and of having access to online banking. When any one of these three officers (or the Faculty Advisor, should he have access) changes, the account shall be updated. Prior to the second meeting of the academic year, all required officers shall be added to the chapter treasury and all exiting officers removed. SECTION FOUR. Money Access The Treasurer, President, Vice President, if he so desires, and Faculty Advisor, if he so desires, shall have the sole authority to write checks or use bank issued Debit Cards on behalf of the fraternity. Should either the Treasurer, President, or Vice President deem it a necessary or prudent expenditure, he may also approve the use of the chapter Debit Card to be used by another member, with the stipulation that the member promptly return the debit card and an itemized receipt for said expenditure. ARTICLE IV. Officers SECTION ONE. Qualifications In addition to the qualifications for officers in Article IV, Section Two of the Bylaws, Title 3: Chapter of Phi Mu Alpha Sinfonia, no member of the chapter may hold more than one chapter office at one time with the exception of the Music Coordinator. An alumni member of the chapter may run for any chapter office; however, he must pay collegiate dues if he holds any office other than Alumni Relations Officer. SECTION TWO. Music Coordinator In addition to those offices denoted in Article IV of the Bylaws, Title 3: Chapter of Phi Mu Alpha Sinfonia, The Beta Sigma Chapter has created the office of Music Coordinator. For officer duties see Article V, Section Ten of these bylaws. SECTION THREE. Order of Succession The order of succession of officers of the Beta Sigma Chapter shall be: the President, the Vice President, the Secretary, the Fraternity Education Officer, the Warden, the Treasurer, the Alumni Relations Officer, the Historian, then the Music Coordinator. If none of these officers are present, then a straw-poll vote shall be taken to appoint a collegiate member in good standing – chosen by a simple majority vote – to assume leadership of the event. This succession shall be called upon for such reasons as to determine who will lead meetings in the President’s absence, etc. ARTICLE V. Officer Duties SECTION ONE. General Regulations Chapter officers will act in accordance with the duties listed in Article IV of the Bylaws, Title 3: Chapter of Phi Mu Alpha Sinfonia. SECTION TWO. President In addition to those duties listed in the Guide to Chapter President and Vice President Duties, the President shall hold the final say in matters of rules of order. 	 SECTION THREE. Vice President The Vice President shall perform those duties listed in the Guide to Chapter President and Vice President Duties. SECTION FOUR. Secretary The Secretary shall maintain physical and digital records containing all minutes, agendas, and other paperwork. He shall also email minutes in a clean, professional format to the chapter no later than 48 hours after the meeting for which they were taken. SECTION FIVE. Fraternity Education Officer In addition to those duties listed in the Guide to Membership Development, the Fraternity Education Officer shall present a calendar of his intentions for that semester’s probationary recruitment by the second meeting of the academic semester. He shall also keep a record of the semester for that semester’s er SECTION SIX. Warden In addition to those duties listed in the Guide to Chapter Warden’s Duties, the Warden shall be in charge of enforcing the accountability policies (Article VIII of these bylaws) and shall have his attendance book at every event. He shall also be in charge of the chapter contact list. SECTION SEVEN. Treasurer In addition to those duties listed in Article IV, Section Eight of the Bylaws, Title 3: Chapter of Phi Mu Alpha Sinfonia and The Guide to Money Management, the Treasurer shall be in charge of keeping track of chapter funds, and able to give an accurate report on the available amount of chapter funds at any given time. The Treasurer shall present a monthly report to the Executive Committee, utilizing bank statements, etc. The Treasurer is also in charge of the chapter PayPal Account. SECTION EIGHT. Alumni Relations Officer In addition to those duties listed in the Guide to Chapter Alumni Relations Officer’s Duties, the Alumni Relations Officer shall receive an updated email address from graduating brothers following the Ceremony for Graduating Brothers. SECTION NINE. Historian In addition to those duties listed in the Guide to Chapter Historian’ Chapter, the Historian shall record the events and lineage of the chapter during each semester in detail, using whatever visual aids he deems necessary. If the Historian cannot attend an event, he shall delegate his duties to a suitable replacement. He shall store each semester’s documentation in both physical and digital form, using a system that is easily used and understood by any member of the fraternity. He will also present collected documents to the chapter on dates determined by the chapter each semester. SECTION TEN. Music Coordinator The Beta Sigma Chapter designates that the Music Coordinator shall adhere to those duties listed in the Guide to Chapter President’s and Vice President’s Duties, page 8. He will also interface with the Social Committee in planning social and fraternal events involving the chapter choir. SECTION ELEVEN. Faculty Advisor The Faculty Advisor shall be encouraged to attend at least one chapter event per semester. ARTICLE VI. Committees SECTION ONE. Executive Committee In accordance with Article IV, Section 14 of the Bylaws, Title 3: Chapter of Phi Mu Alpha Sinfonia, the Executive Committee for the Beta Sigma Chapter has been defined as the President, the Vice President, the Secretary, the Fraternity Education Officer, the Warden, and the Treasurer. SECTION TWO. General Committee Structure The Beta Sigma Chapter has designated the continuing existence of the following committees. Each committee is expected to meet consistently and give regular progress reports to the executive committee. The Vice President is responsible for overseeing the committees. SUBSECTION ONE. Social The Social Committee is to aid the chapter in its relationship with the University, Lionel Hampton School of Music, and the community at large. They shall be in charge of event planning and public relations. The Social Committee Chair shall act as a liaison between the committee and the Executive Committee, with the aid of the Music Coordinator and/or Secretary. SUBSECTION TWO. Fundraising The Fundraising Committee is to aid in the gathering of funds for the chapterrsity, Lionel HamptoTreasurer shall act as a liaison between the committee and the Executive Committee. SUBSECTION THREE. Special Committees In addition to the committees listed above, the chapter may form special committees for specific tasks on an as-needed basis. This includes, but is not limited to, committees for specific events such as the Ridenbaugh Haunted House or Scrubfest. ARTICLE VII. Special Events and Observances SECTION ONE. Recital In addition to the American Music Program required under Article II, Section 6 of the Bylaws, Title 3: Chapter of Phi Mu Alpha Sinfonia that will be held in the fall, the Beta Sigma Chapter will hold a recital in the spring. SECTION TWO. Mills Music Mission The Beta Sigma Chapter shall annually present at least one Mills Music Mission to the community in addition to those required for probationary membership and province workshop. SECTION THREE. Formal Attire / Letters Day Members of the Beta Sigma Chapter are encouraged to wear formal pin attire every other Wednesday of the academic year, while wearing fraternity letters on the interspersing Wednesdays, beginning with formal pin attire on the first Wednesday of the academic semester. Sinfonia Cup The Beta Sigma Chapter shall hold a so-named of the academic year, while wearing fraternity letters on the interspersing Wednesdays, beginning with formal pin attire on the first Wednesda SECTION FIVE. Haunted House The Beta Sigma Chapter shall, every year that it is held, participate in a haunted house every Halloween season for the benefit of the Moscow Food Bank. SECTION SIX. Scrubfest The Beta Sigma Chapter shall host the Ridenbaugh Scrubfest prior to the Lionel Hampton School of Music every HallowDay. SECTION SEVEN. LyreQuest The Beta Sigma Chapter is encouraged to, no less than every three years (barring a national convention), attend a retreat at LyreCrest. Any Sinfonian in good standing with both the chapter and the fraternity nationally may take part in this expedition. SECTION EIGHT. Lionel Hampton Jazz Festival The Beta Sigma Chapter shall volunteer at the Lionel Hampton Jazz Festival every spring semester. The Chapter is encouraged to manage their own site at the festival. ARTICLE VIII. Discipline SECTION ONE. Attendance Should a collegiate member accrue three unexcused absences from events deemed mandatory, the Executive Committee shall send a notice requesting communication from that member via email. Should absences persist, it shall be considered grounds for suspension in accordance with Article IX, Section One of the Bylaws, Title 3: Chapter of Phi Mu Alpha Sinfonia., it shall be considered may review the Wardeninfonia., it shall be per the committee three weeks . Reasons for planned absences must be submitted in writing to the official chapter email address (betasigmabulls@gmail.com) no later than 10 days prior to the planned absence of a mandatory event. Unplanned absences must be submitted in writing no later than 48 hours prior to event. All other cases will be handled on a case by case basis. SECTION TWO. Dues See Article III of these bylaws for the disciplinary policy involving dues. SECTION THREE. Chapter Suspension Members of the Beta Sigma Chapter may be placed on suspension by the chapter in accordance with Article IX of the Bylaws, Title 3: Chapter of Phi Mu Alpha Sinfonia. Members on chapter suspension may or may not be on suspension with the fraternity nationally. Members on chapter suspension must attend meetings, but may not take part or have their vote counted on any issues. They may not attend social events. SECTION FOUR. Expulsion See Article IX, Section Three of the Bylaws, Title 3: Chapter of Phi Mu Alpha Sinfonia. ARTICLE IX. Miscellaneous Chapter Procedures SECTION ONE. Chapter Communication The Beta Sigma Chapter designates that any fraternity-related communication between any member and the Executive Committee must be submitted via email to the official chapter email address (betasigmabulls@gmail.com) or the chapter mailbox in the Lionel Hampton School of Music. SECTION TWO. Voting Procedures The official voting procedure of the Beta Sigma Chapter shall be as follows: Chapter quorum shall be in accordance with Article VIII, Section Two of the Bylaws, Title 3: Chapter of Phi Mu Alpha Sinfonia. A two-thirds quorum vote shall decide the issue at hand. Should the issue be unresolved, the floor will open for a discussion of no more than ten minutes, after which a second two-thirds quorum vote shall take place. Should the issue remain unresolved, it may be resubmitted and reviewed at a later date. In the case of personnel elections, the above procedure shall take place with the provision of a simple majority quorum vote. ARTICLE X. Amendments and Reviews SECTION ONE. Amendments These bylaws may be amended at any regular business meeting, provided that the proposed amendment was presented in writing prior to the meeting. See Article IX, Section II of these bylaws for the voting procedure. SECTION TWO. Reviews These bylaws shall be reviewed at least once every academic year and following any major changes to the governing documents listed in Article I, Section Two of these bylaws. These updated bylaws shall be reviewed no later than December following a National Assembly. ARTICLE XI. University of Idaho Policies SECTION ONE. Non-Discrimination Policy The University of Idaho has a policy of nondiscrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, or status as a Vietnam era veteran. This policy applies to all programs, services, and facilities, and includes, but is not limited to, applications, admissions, access to programs and services, and employment. SECTION TWO.
